name: Pulmonary Veno-Occlusive Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal universally accepted criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, radiologic, and histopathologic findings

criteria.description: Presence of pulmonary hypertension confirmed by right heart catheterization
Characteristic high-resolution CT findings including centrilobular ground-glass opacities, septal lines, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy
Histological evidence of widespread occlusion of small pulmonary veins
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension such as left heart disease or chronic thromboembolic disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical pulmonary hypertension with characteristic radiologic features and exclusion of other causes; histopathologic confirmation if available
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Lung biopsy is definitive but often high risk; diagnosis often presumptive based on clinical and imaging findings

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension confirmed by right heart catheterization

laboratory: Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
imaging: High-resolution CT showing centrilobular ground-glass opacities
genetic: Mutations in EIF2AK4 gene associated with familial cases
other: Right heart catheterization demonstrating elevated pulmonary arterial pressures with normal wedge pressure

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of venous obstruction on histology
Different radiologic pattern without septal lines or lymphadenopathy
Presence of thromboembolic material on imaging
Echocardiographic evidence of left heart dysfunction

redFlags: Rapid progression of pulmonary hypertension symptoms
Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
Development of pulmonary edema with vasodilator therapy
references: Montani D, et al. Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease. Eur Respir J. 2009;33(1):189-200.
Eyries M, et al. EIF2AK4 mutations cause pulmonary veno-occlusive disease, a recessive form of pulmonary hypertension. Nat Genet. 2014;46(1):65-69.
Simonneau G, et al. Updated clinical classification of pulmonary hypertension. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2013;62(25 Suppl):D34-D41.
